page.name: Sending straight from a provider vs through a layer
page.h1: Sending straight from your provider vs through an orchestration layer
page.metaTitle: Direct provider sending vs an orchestration layer
page.metaDescription: What the layer adds once more than one team or account has to send coherently: one integration, cross-provider routing, one normalized status.
page.lede: Sending direct is the fastest way to send the first message. The layer is what keeps messaging dependable once a second provider, a second team or a second failure arrives — and it adds nothing you have to migrate away from.

sections.h: What the layer adds on top of direct sending
bullets: One integration across providers instead of one per provider, with one place every team sends from
Cross-provider routing, failover and pacing handled at the layer rather than rebuilt by each team (SMS channel)
One normalized status, so a receipt means the same thing whichever account carried the message
Suppression held in one place and applied consistently, wherever a send originates

sections.h: How the layer fits alongside direct sending
p: The layer does not replace direct sending — it sits above it. Your provider keeps its own features and you keep one relationship; what the layer adds is the cross-provider behavior a single direct integration cannot give you, and adopting it later is a matter of connecting accounts rather than renegotiating anything.

Start direct, and add the layer when more than one team or more than one account has to send coherently. Because the accounts stay yours, the layer is a configuration you add and can remove — not a migration you commit to on day one.

faq.q: Do we lose provider features by going through a layer?
faq.a: The layer carries the capabilities it implements for each connection, and the integrations pages list them per provider — so the answer is checkable rather than assumed. Anything the layer does not carry, your provider account still does, directly.

faq.q: Can we start direct and move later?
faq.a: Yes, and that is often the right order. Because the accounts stay yours, adopting the layer later means connecting them rather than renegotiating anything.

faq.q: What happens to our provider-specific setup?
faq.a: It stays exactly where it is. The layer sends through the account you already configured and reads status back from it, so nothing about your provider setup has to change to try it.
